correctness.rationale: Every right inverse is represented by vertex-data coefficient measures of total mass one. Exact KR duality on the equilateral vertex metric gives half-l1 column differences. Permutation averaging reduces the unrestricted minimum to weights a inside and b outside each k-face. Exhaustive geometric pair types give exactly A(b), B(b), C(b),1. Signed b outside [0,1/n] cannot improve the optimum. The A/B versus A/C crossing comparison is equivalent to sqrt(r) versus p+q; p^2+q^2=1 forces the sharp codimension split. Explicit positive coefficients attain the optimum. Fixed-k derivative signs yield the strict limiting envelope; differentiation and exact rational square bounds certify its unique integer maximum k=17. Direct exhaustive pair tests pass 38,544 instances of point pairs over 21 parameters; four fully nonsymmetric HiGHS linear programs independently agree. Computations are corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem has a canonical object (all equal-cardinality face barycenters of a regular simplex), a standard functional-analytic invariant (minimum linear Lipschitz extension norm), a fully determined positive optimizer and dimension/codimension branches. The unique cardinality-17 global limiting maximum is a nontrivial and unexpected structural phenomenon, established analytically rather than by isolated tabulation. This supplies calibrated simultaneous interpolation stability bounds and an exact finite-metric complementability benchmark, beyond a narrow substitution or routine numerical example.
